summary.headline: Zee Q2 FY27 operating revenue up 13% YoY, with FIFA-driven digital revenue doubling; EBITDA margin fell to 3.2% on new-initiative spends.
summary.overview: Management reported 13% YoY growth in operating revenues, attributed mainly to the sports business (FIFA World Cup on ZEE5 and Unite8 Sports). ZEE5 revenues more than doubled YoY and grew 37% QoQ to INR6.3 billion, the highest quarterly digital revenue to date. EBITDA was INR708 million with a 3.2% margin, hit by FIFA programming and advertising costs and marketing spends on new initiatives (Bullet, KidZ, sports); management said the margin would have been mid-to-high single digit excluding those spends. PAT was INR456 million. Advertising was flat YoY and up 20% QoQ, and management said the ad decline has stabilised.

financial_highlights.value: Up 13% YoY (absolute figure not stated in call)

financial_highlights.change: Mid-to-high single digit ex new-initiative spends
After investments in sports and new initiatives

financial_highlights.value: INR25.7 billion (bank INR5.3bn, FDs and other INR11bn, mutual funds INR9.4bn)
financial_highlights.change: Includes first tranche of INR7.4bn from promoter preferential warrants
-36% YoY on higher syndication in base year

segments.name: Digital (ZEE5)
segments.commentary: Revenue more than doubled YoY and grew 37% QoQ to INR6.3 billion; digital EBITDA INR416 million after marketing and platform investments. Management expects digital momentum to continue in H2.

segments.name: Linear broadcast
segments.commentary: Management described the linear business as stable; network share was 20% as of week 24, the highest in seven years, but ratings measurement is currently paused. Management said linear subscription growth was stable and that the full sports benefit will show in FY28 as deals are fixed.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Flat YoY, helped by FIFA, Sa Re Ga Ma Pa and new launches; up 20% QoQ as Middle East uncertainty eased. Festive season shifted into Q3 this year.

segments.name: Music
segments.commentary: Over 59 billion total video views and more than 179 million YouTube subscribers; management says profitability remains healthy. Segment disclosure is still withheld.

segments.name: Movies / studio
segments.commentary: Released six movies in Q2 (one Hindi, five other languages). Other sales and services fell 36% YoY against a higher syndication deal in the base year. Acquired international distribution rights to Drishyam 3, released in Q3.

segments.name: Sports
segments.commentary: FIFA full-tournament reach grew about 41% vs the previous World Cup, with about 83% of viewership live on ZEE5 and total reach above 400 million. Rights acquired to FIFA until 2034, plus Bundesliga and Serie A for five years.

guidance_outlook: Subscription revenue growth to accelerate from H2 onwards versus normalised levels, but not at the 30% seen in Q2 (management).
About 35% to 40% of FIFA-acquired subscribers retained after the event, with most renewing for another quarter or longer; accrual benefit continues through Q3 and Q4.
Management expects advertising revenue to hold without further decline in H2, with encouraging festive-season signs.
Digital growth momentum expected to continue in H2; marketing spends on new initiatives expected to pay off in H2 through subscription pack renewals.
Management said the true financial impact of new sports rights will be visible in FY28, since current linear deals are already fixed.
Management remains cautiously optimistic on FY27 revenue growth and profitability, citing festive season and content slate for Q3 and Q4.
capex_capacity: Ongoing investment in ZEE5 platform revamp across mobile and connected TV, with AI-led discovery and a stronger personalisation engine.
Bullet launched Trinetra AI, an end-to-end AI filmmaking and content intelligence platform aimed at the micro-drama segment.
Investment phase in kids, live experiences, animated content, micro dramas and sports, with new businesses still in investment mode.
Received INR7.4 billion, the first tranche of preferential warrant proceeds from promoters; FCCB repayment and dividend payout weighed on cash in the quarter.
demand_pricing: FIFA-driven subscriptions were mainly quarterly packs; revised FIFA pricing aided ZEE5 growth.
Linear pricing increases contributed to subscription growth, alongside digital ARPU and subscriber growth.
Omni reach across genres crossed 800 million monthly; ZEE5 released 34 shows and movies, including nine original series, in the quarter.
Advertising was flat YoY, and management cited high inflation and a weak monsoon as subdued macro headwinds.
Competition: management says Zee is India's number 2 TV entertainment network; it claims top digital engagement on YouTube and Meta in key language markets, per third-party data.

qa_highlights.question: How much did FIFA contribute to linear and ZEE5 revenue, and what would the quarter look like without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not quantify FIFA revenue but said it was 'quite healthy', mostly booked as subscription. Linear revenue was stable, and the true sports benefit will show in FY28 because current deals are fixed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for withholding Zee Music segment disclosure, and is there a timeline for value unlocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working on segment reporting for the whole company rather than piecemeal and will revert when the time is right; it gave no timeline, citing investment-mode businesses.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the rise in receivables and inventories, and how did that affect cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivables are cyclical with no build-up affecting cash. Cash was mainly hit by the FCCB payment and dividend payout. Inventory includes show builds to be released in coming quarters, and inventory fell slightly QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: After FIFA, where will subscription growth settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention of FIFA subscribers is 35% to 40%, with renewals for quarterly and longer packs. Subscription growth will accelerate from normalised levels in H2, but not to 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Note 10 operating expense a one-off, and what is the status of legal cases?
qa_highlights.answer: Note 10 relates to a prior-year (Q4 FY26) transaction, shown for reference only, with no impact on Q2 margin. The main legal matter is the ICC case; management cannot predict timing for the LCIA arbitration.

risks_watch: Subscription growth will slow once FIFA-driven packs normalise; the 35% to 40% retention rate is the key indicator to track.
EBITDA margin of 3.2% depends on how much new-initiative spend continues (Bullet, KidZ, sports, digital marketing).
Ratings measurement is paused, so the 20% network share is not verified by current industry data.
Segment disclosure (music) is still withheld with no timeline, and the value-unlock question is open.
Pending legal matters, including the ICC case and LCIA arbitration, have no timeline.
Cash balance was reduced by the FCCB repayment and dividend; watch the second tranche of warrant proceeds and working capital (receivables, show inventory).
summary.management_tone: Confident on digital and sports momentum, but cautious on profitability and guidance. Management gave no numbers for FIFA revenue, segment reporting, or the timing of legal outcomes, and used qualitative answers where pressed.
key_quotes: I'm glad to share that ZEE5's revenues doubled year-on-year, charting a strong growth trajectory.
As a result of these costs, EBITDA margin for the quarter was 3.2%.
We can't predict these deadlines on the basis of what the court may do or may not do or what even the other side party may do.

growth.why: Management guides subscription growth to accelerate from H2 (below the 30% seen in Q2) and advertising to hold without further decline in H2, backed by FIFA subscriber retention of 35-40%, linear pricing and ZEE5 digital momentum; no specific capacity or order numbers were given, and management is only cautiously optimistic on FY27 growth.
